title: Follow a nearby moving star

frames.wavelength_location: Spectral WCS (key W) sampled at the catalog-predicted position of Barnard's Star at this frame's mid-exposure time (native pixel x=28.33, y=30.00). Other pixels in the image record other wavelengths.
limitations: Display image is nearest-neighbour resampled from ~6.15 arcsec native pixels onto a 256x256 grid of 1.406 arcsec display pixels; it adds no resolution.
Pixels are contrast-stretched for viewing only; no background subtraction; not photometry.
The quality screen checks flags in a small circle around one position. A clear result is not a detection.
The marker is a catalog prediction, not a position measured in this image.

claim: UI verification: a visible shift deserves a quality check before making a motion claim.
observations: The dated observations and wavelength labels remain attached to the comparison.
uncertainty: Flagged pixels near the predicted target limit precise position and brightness claims.
case_limitations: The star's center is saturated (OVERFLOW/BLOOM flags) in all retained frames; no centroid or brightness measurement is supported.
Frames A and B are from Data Release 1 and frame C from Quick Release 3; quick-release products may be reprocessed later.
The marker is a catalog prediction from SIMBAD/Gaia astrometry, not a measured position. Annual parallax (about 0.55 arcsec) is not modeled.

The visible shift is under two SPHEREx pixels (about 7 display pixels); it depends on correct alignment to a fixed sky grid, which was checked against Gaia field stars (stable to under 1 display pixel; see verification).
The glow's center can only be judged by eye: saturated pixels have no value, and a visual estimate of the glow center scatters by about 1 display pixel from frame to frame.
